name: payment_frequency:bonus_score
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.41 is high and warrants inclusion. The interaction is commercially meaningful: monthly payers with low bonus scores may be systematically underpriced if only main effects are used. Recommend validating with lift charts segmented by payment_frequency x bonus_score band before finalising relativities.

name: occupants_premium:business_type
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.34 is strong. This interaction is defensible: the occupants premium loading should differ between personal and commercial/fleet policies. Ensure the interaction is parameterised consistently with the occupants coverage underwriting rules.

name: property_damage_premium:liability_premium
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.30 is material. The interaction reflects the correlation between third-party and own-damage risk for the same driver. However, care is needed to avoid double-counting with policy_type main effect. Recommend checking VIF and partial dependence plots.

name: vehicle_value:bonus_score
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.29 is material and the interaction is actuarially intuitive. Regulatorily defensible as it reflects genuine risk compounding. Recommend banding vehicle_value into quantile groups for the interaction term to improve stability.

name: fire_premium:bonus_score
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.28 is notable. The actuarial rationale is plausible but somewhat indirect — bonus score primarily reflects accident history, not fire behaviour. Recommend including but monitoring for overfitting. Consider whether the signal persists after controlling for vehicle_age and fuel_type.

name: bonus_score:vehicle_age
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.27 is material. Actuarially justified: the combination of vehicle age and claims history provides meaningful risk segmentation. Recommend validating that the interaction is not confounded with vehicle_value (older vehicles tend to be lower value).

name: legal_protection_premium:business_type
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.27 is strong and the interaction is actuarially and regulatorily defensible. Ensure the interaction relativities are consistent with the legal protection product terms for commercial vs. personal policies.

name: vehicle_age:driver_age
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.13 is moderate but the actuarial rationale is very strong and well-documented in motor insurance literature. This interaction should be retained on actuarial grounds even if the H-statistic alone would not prioritise it highly. Recommend banding both variables for the interaction term.

name: policy_type:payment_frequency
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.13 is moderate. The interaction is commercially plausible. Recommend validating with observed loss ratios segmented by policy_type x payment_frequency before including in production model.

name: payment_frequency:driver_age
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.12 is moderate. The actuarial rationale is plausible but the interaction may partially overlap with payment_frequency:bonus_score. Recommend checking for collinearity between these two interactions before including both.

name: driver_age:glass_premium
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.12 is moderate. The actuarial rationale is plausible but glass claims are high-frequency low-severity and may introduce noise. Recommend validating with observed glass claim rates by driver age band before including.

name: theft_premium:payment_frequency
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.12 is moderate. The actuarial rationale is indirect — payment frequency is not a direct driver of theft risk. This interaction may be partially spurious or driven by confounding with municipality_type. Recommend including only if it survives a partial dependence validation and does not conflict with regulatory guidance on socioeconomic proxies.

name: bonus_score:driver_age
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.11 is moderate but the actuarial rationale is strong. This interaction is standard in markets with bonus-malus systems. Recommend including with appropriate banding of driver_age.

name: property_damage_premium:policy_type
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.11 is moderate. This interaction has a clear structural justification: property damage premiums should be interpreted differently depending on whether the policy includes own-damage coverage. Recommend including as it improves model consistency with product structure.

name: vehicle_value:policy_type
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.105 is at the threshold. The actuarial rationale is sound and the interaction is regulatorily defensible. Recommend including.

name: liability_premium:policy_type
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.102 is at the threshold. The interaction is structurally justified by product design. Recommend including but monitoring for collinearity with property_damage_premium:policy_type.

name: payment_frequency:business_type
actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.101 is at the threshold. The actuarial rationale is plausible but indirect. This interaction may overlap with occupants_premium:business_type. Recommend including provisionally and reviewing in model validation.

name: fuel_type:seats
actuary_note: Highest H-statistic (0.458). The interaction is plausible because fuel type and seat count jointly define vehicle segment (e.g., electric SUV vs. petrol city car vs. diesel minibus), each with distinct repair cost and frequency profiles. Recommend validating with one-way lift charts by fuel_type within each seat band.

name: policy_type:bonus_score
actuary_note: Second highest H-statistic (0.358). Strong actuarial rationale: bonus score sensitivity to claims history differs by policy type due to coverage scope and adverse selection. Regulatorily defensible as both variables are standard rating factors. Recommend checking for sufficient exposure in all cells.

name: power_to_weight_ratio:seats
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.330. Actuarially justified as the combination of performance metric and vehicle size defines vehicle segment risk. Ensure sufficient data in high power-to-weight, high seat count cells to avoid overfitting.

name: theft_premium:bonus_score
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.313. Actuarially plausible: policyholders with poor bonus scores in high-theft areas represent compounded risk. However, note that theft_premium is itself a pre-computed score, so care is needed to avoid double-counting. Recommend reviewing the construction of theft_premium to confirm independence from bonus_score.

name: policy_type:theft_premium
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.312. Strong actuarial justification: theft coverage is only present in certain policy types, so the theft premium should interact with policy type. This is arguably a structural interaction that should be included regardless of H-statistic. Regulatorily very defensible.

name: power_to_weight_ratio:vehicle_brand
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.305. Actuarially justified but implementation complexity is high given the number of brand levels. Consider grouping vehicle brands into risk tiers before implementing this interaction to maintain GLM parsimony and avoid sparse cells.

name: vehicle_brand:seats
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.290. Reasonable actuarial basis but may create many sparse cells when combined with vehicle_brand levels. Recommend brand grouping or using a brand risk index before implementing. Monitor for overfitting.

name: bonus_score:municipality_type
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.249. Actuarially plausible as claims frequency base rates differ by municipality type, affecting how bonus score translates to risk. Regulatorily defensible. Recommend validating with partial dependence plots stratified by municipality type.

name: municipality_type:circulation_area
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.215. Strong actuarial and regulatory justification as geographic risk is inherently hierarchical. This interaction effectively creates a finer territorial grid. Ensure sufficient exposure in all geographic cells.

name: bonus_score:payment_frequency
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.208. The interaction has a plausible behavioural basis (financial stress correlating with both monthly payment and poor bonus score), but it is partially data-driven. Recommend including with caution and monitoring for stability across validation periods. Ensure it does not act as a proxy for a protected characteristic.

name: fuel_type:vehicle_brand
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.205. Actuarially justified for vehicle risk segmentation. Implementation should account for the fact that not all fuel type × brand combinations exist in the portfolio. Sparse cells should be grouped or regularised.

name: vehicle_brand:municipality_type
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.177. Actuarially plausible but creates a large number of cells. Recommend brand grouping before implementation. Monitor for data sparsity.

name: policy_type:vehicle_age
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.174. Strong actuarial rationale: the depreciation effect on insured value is only relevant for own-damage covers (comprehensive/TPFT), making this a structurally important interaction. Regulatorily defensible.

name: power_to_weight_ratio:fuel_type
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.160. Actuarially justified and increasingly important as EV penetration grows. The interaction helps avoid mispricing high-performance EVs relative to equivalent petrol vehicles.

name: power_to_weight_ratio:age_driving_licence
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.148. Very strong actuarial justification — the interaction of inexperience and vehicle performance is a well-established risk amplifier. Regulatorily defensible and commonly included in motor pricing models.

name: bonus_score:driver_age
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.143. Actuarially justified: bonus score credibility increases with driving history length, which correlates with driver age. This interaction is regulatorily defensible as it improves risk discrimination without introducing protected characteristic proxies.

name: theft_premium:driver_age
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.141. Moderate actuarial justification. The interaction is plausible but partially data-driven. Recommend including only if it shows consistent lift in out-of-sample validation. Monitor for stability.

name: seats:circulation_area
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.138. Moderate actuarial justification. The interaction captures urban vs. rural risk differences by vehicle type. Recommend validating with exposure-weighted lift charts.

name: theft_premium:payment_frequency
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.132. Partially data-driven. The interaction may act as a socioeconomic proxy. Recommend careful review to ensure it does not indirectly discriminate against protected groups. Include only if actuarial lift is demonstrated in validation and legal review is satisfactory.

name: vehicle_value:vehicle_brand
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.131. Actuarially justified for severity modelling. However, vehicle value and brand are correlated, so the interaction may be partially redundant. Recommend checking VIF and ensuring the interaction adds genuine lift beyond main effects.

name: vehicle_value:power_to_weight_ratio
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.130. Actuarially justified for premium vehicle risk segmentation. Ensure the interaction does not create instability in sparse high-value, high-performance cells.

name: payment_frequency:driver_age
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.124. Partially behavioural and potentially a socioeconomic proxy. Recommend legal and compliance review to ensure this does not indirectly discriminate. Include only if validated actuarial lift is demonstrated.

name: vehicle_value:bonus_score
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.122. Actuarially justified: the combination of high vehicle value and poor claims history is a known high-risk segment. Regulatorily defensible.

name: theft_premium:business_type
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.122. Actuarially justified: commercial use changes the theft risk profile significantly. Regulatorily defensible.

name: seats:age_driving_licence
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.121. Moderate actuarial justification. The interaction is plausible but less structurally obvious than power_to_weight_ratio:age_driving_licence. Include if validation confirms lift.

name: vehicle_value:theft_premium
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.121. Strong actuarial justification for theft coverage. Note that theft_premium may already incorporate vehicle value to some degree — review the construction of theft_premium to avoid double-counting.

name: policy_type:payment_frequency
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.116. Partially data-driven. The interaction may reflect commercial pricing structures (instalment loadings varying by policy type) rather than pure risk differentiation. Recommend reviewing whether this is a risk or commercial pricing term.

name: municipality_type:business_type
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.116. Actuarially justified for commercial vehicle risk segmentation. Regulatorily defensible.

name: bonus_score:age_driving_licence
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.112. Actuarially justified but note that bonus_score and age_driving_licence are correlated. The interaction may be partially redundant with main effects. Recommend checking for multicollinearity and validating incremental lift.

name: vehicle_value:payment_frequency
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.111. Partially data-driven and potentially a socioeconomic proxy. Recommend legal review and validation before inclusion. The interaction may reflect commercial instalment loading structures rather than pure risk.

name: driver_age:seats
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.111. Moderate actuarial justification. Similar rationale to power_to_weight_ratio:age_driving_licence but weaker. Include if validation confirms incremental lift over existing interactions.

name: theft_premium:power_to_weight_ratio
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.110. Borderline actuarial justification. The interaction is plausible but may be partially data-driven. Recommend including only if out-of-sample validation confirms consistent lift. Flag for monitoring.

name: vehicle_value:driver_age
actuary_note: H-statistic 0.109. Strong actuarial justification. Regulatorily defensible as both variables are standard rating factors. Recommend including.
